method: tools/lanec/cover.py: every host case of each suite run alone through build/lanec-cover/lanec-native (-O0 --coverage, with LANEC_COVER_SITES so each call of a shared helper (lanec_ccs, lanec_ccs_a, lanec_ts, lanec_ev_zero, lanec_ev_nonpositive, lanec_ev_mp) branches on its outcome at the call line) and the branch arcs it takes in every linked source read with gcov -b (tools/c64_row_cover.py); the C64 rows are the cases frozen in tests/lanec_<suite>_c64.h (every case when the suite has none), and their arcs are compared with the whole host suite's; with --pool, a host arc of one suite counts as taken on the C64 when the C64 rows of any suite in the record take it (the same source line and branch in the same build)
pooled_only: these host suites have no C64 rows of their own: the suite named in c64_rows_in runs the same cases one routine at a time through the flight modules as the C64 module test does, and its frozen rows run on the C64 (make vice-lanec-pin-chains); their arcs count as taken on the C64 only through the pool

host_only_lines.tests/lanec_pin_head.c:28: The transfer harness scans a pin-head family once per program and reuses the scan for later rows (the cache lookup on this line). Only pin-transfer-c64 rows of the pin-head programs take these arcs, and all 16 pin-head transfer programs pass $C000 (LANEC_PIN_C64_TOO_BIG), so their rows run in the flight store instead. This is test-harness code, not port code; the pin-head modules run on the C64 in the pin-head suites own programs.
